evidence.claim: EAC leaders agreed to send a regional force to the DRC, called for an immediate ceasefire, and said the force would work with DRC military and administrative authorities to stabilise the east.
evidence.title: East Africa leaders agree regional force to quell DR Congo crisis
evidence.excerpt: EAC leaders agreed to send a regional force to the DRC, called for an immediate ceasefire, and said the force would work with DRC military and administrative authorities to stabilise the east.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters-sourced regional diplomacy report with explicit meeting outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Tshisekedi was a direct participant in the summit, but the decision was regional rather than unilateral.
contrary_evidence: This is diplomacy around an inherited conflict, not proof of durable implementation.

evidence.claim: The Luanda mini-summit produced a ceasefire to take effect on 25 November and required M23 to withdraw from occupied areas in the DRC.
evidence.title: Le mini-sommet de Luanda impose au m23/Rwanda un cessez-le-feu et le retrait des zones occupées en RDC
evidence.excerpt: The Luanda mini-summit produced a ceasefire to take effect on 25 November and required M23 to withdraw from occupied areas in the DRC.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidency communiqué on a dated regional agreement in which Tshisekedi participated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Tshisekedi's participation in a regional settlement effort.
contrary_evidence: Agreement terms do not establish compliance or long-term peace.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi said M23 had to stop hostilities, withdraw from its positions, and return to its November 2021 lines as a condition for joining the Nairobi peace process.
evidence.title: Troisième phase des pourparlers de Nairobi : Les chefs d’Etats appellent les groupes armés à déposer les armes
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi said M23 had to stop hostilities, withdraw from its positions, and return to its November 2021 lines as a condition for joining the Nairobi peace process.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct quotation of Tshisekedi in contemporaneous local-language reporting on the Nairobi process.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler statement during peace negotiations
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own public peace-process position.
contrary_evidence: This is a stated condition for talks, not proof that the condition was enforceable.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with explicit policy attribution and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this describes the national authorities under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: The same release says poverty remained very high and domestic arrears accumulated.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Budget's 2022 budget page shows the law on finances for 2022, Law No. 21/029 of 31 December 2021, and the linked budget documents for 2022.
evidence.title: Budget 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Budget's 2022 budget page shows the law on finances for 2022, Law No. 21/029 of 31 December 2021, and the linked budget documents for 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official budget portal with the named 2022 finance law.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is the incumbent government's approved fiscal framework.
contrary_evidence: Budget approval alone does not establish implementation quality.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a project to increase mining revenue transparency and strengthen expenditure management at the central level and in selected provinces so that more funds reach public service delivery.
evidence.title: World Bank Supports the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Efforts to Improve Public Resources Management and Service Delivery
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a project to increase mining revenue transparency and strengthen expenditure management at the central level and in selected provinces so that more funds reach public service delivery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank project announcement with direct fiscal-governance objective.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 reform baseline for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is a government-supported reform package in the Tshisekedi period.
contrary_evidence: The project was approved because the underlying revenue and expenditure systems still needed strengthening.

evidence.claim: The project would support a single treasury account, better budget control, improved annual reporting, stronger oversight by the Court of Accounts, and enhanced civil-society participation in budgeting.
evidence.title: World Bank Supports the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Efforts to Improve Public Resources Management and Service Delivery
evidence.excerpt: The project would support a single treasury account, better budget control, improved annual reporting, stronger oversight by the Court of Accounts, and enhanced civil-society participation in budgeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary project design statement with concrete institutional reforms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the reforms are tied to the incumbent government's public financial management agenda.
contrary_evidence: The statement itself implies the reforms were still needed, so this is not evidence of success by itself.

evidence.claim: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent international validation of disclosure practices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: strong institutional transparency evidence, but not a direct measure of household welfare.
contrary_evidence: The same decision says beneficial ownership and some newer standards were not yet fully implemented.

evidence.claim: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent validation report with a concrete quantitative gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is about extractive-sector transparency under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some progress in open-format disclosure.

evidence.claim: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.title: I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary investigative reporting with direct recording-based allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the conduct was tied to a close presidential adviser invoking access to Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The recording appears to be an apparent sting operation, so the evidentiary chain should be kept explicit.

evidence.claim: HRW says Congolese authorities had not meaningfully investigated police involvement in the Buhene killings, and that after martial law came into force President Tshisekedi appointed the police commander in charge of the attacks as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.title: DR Congo: No Inquiry into Police Role in Ethnic Killings
evidence.excerpt: HRW says Congolese authorities had not meaningfully investigated police involvement in the Buhene killings, and that after martial law came into force President Tshisekedi appointed the police commander in charge of the attacks as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: HRW gives a dated, specific account with named officials and a clear attribution chain to the president's appointment decision.
evidence.period_fit: 2022, with retrospective reference to April 2021 events that shaped 2022 accountability choices
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for the appointment and indirect for the failure to investigate; the article ties both to Tshisekedi-era authorities.
contrary_evidence: The underlying violence began in 2021, so the failure is partly inherited.
The article does not prove Tshisekedi personally ordered the non-investigation.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi chaired an evaluation meeting on the 145 territories development program with the prime minister, sector ministers, and partner agencies, and the presidency said the identified projects were ready and the program comprised nearly 200 works such as hospitals and administrative buildings.
evidence.title: Réunion d'évaluation du programme de développement à la base des 145 territoires
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi chaired an evaluation meeting on the 145 territories development program with the prime minister, sector ministers, and partner agencies, and the presidency said the identified projects were ready and the program comprised nearly 200 works such as hospitals and administrative buildings.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official account gives a concrete implementation milestone, though it is still government self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 implementation inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution: the meeting was chaired by Tshisekedi and tied to his named program.
contrary_evidence: Readiness claims are official and not independently audited here.

evidence.claim: The same council meeting says the president credited a completed electrification project at Ipamu to his request and ordered budgetary ministries to pay for other investment projects in the ANSER pipeline.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la cinquante-sixieme reunion du conseil des ministres
evidence.excerpt: The same council meeting says the president credited a completed electrification project at Ipamu to his request and ordered budgetary ministries to pay for other investment projects in the ANSER pipeline.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official minutes provide a concrete implementation and resource-allocation directive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution: the action is described as undertaken at the president's request and under his instruction.
contrary_evidence: A single showcased project may not reflect system-wide execution.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi said the M23 advance had created a humanitarian crisis with more than 200,000 displaced people and that the government had been instructed to gather and care for them.
evidence.title: Adresse a la nation du President de la Republique, Felix Tshisekedi suite a la deterioration de la situation securitaire a l'est du pays
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi said the M23 advance had created a humanitarian crisis with more than 200,000 displaced people and that the government had been instructed to gather and care for them.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential address states the crisis scale and the government's response order.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution: the instruction is explicitly issued by the president during a live crisis.
contrary_evidence: The underlying displacement is a negative external shock, not proof of competence by itself.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the DRC's macroeconomic environment had improved, the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies by halting central bank financing to the government, and further monetary, exchange-rate, natural-resource, and business-climate reforms were needed.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Staff Report for the 2022 Article IV Consultation, Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the DRC's macroeconomic environment had improved, the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies by halting central bank financing to the government, and further monetary, exchange-rate, natural-resource, and business-climate reforms were needed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF staff report is a strong independent macroeconomic source with explicit policy assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 assessment of the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate-to-high attribution: these policies are attributed to the authorities under Tshisekedi, but some constraints are inherited and technocratic.
contrary_evidence: IMF also says more reform is needed, so the record is mixed rather than definitive.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said growth rebounded strongly to 6.2 percent in 2021, but poverty reduction remained elusive; it also said the new telecom law and secondary legislation, fiber backbone investment, PPPs, and tax simplification were priority steps for digital-led growth and job creation.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said growth rebounded strongly to 6.2 percent in 2021, but poverty reduction remained elusive; it also said the new telecom law and secondary legislation, fiber backbone investment, PPPs, and tax simplification were priority steps for digital-led growth and job creation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank press release combines outcome assessment with concrete policy recommendations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate-to-high attribution: macro growth is partly commodity-driven and not fully ruler-owned, but the reform agenda is government-directed.
contrary_evidence: The report says poverty reduction was still elusive and much growth came from mining and external conditions.

evidence.claim: The IGF audit of state mining company Gecamines was commissioned by President Tshisekedi and found severe irregularities, including embezzlement and the disappearance of $414 million that should have reached the central bank.
evidence.title: DR Congo: State Mining Company Subject to a Damning Audit
evidence.excerpt: The IGF audit of state mining company Gecamines was commissioned by President Tshisekedi and found severe irregularities, including embezzlement and the disappearance of $414 million that should have reached the central bank.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent investigative report citing the IGF audit and the president's commissioning of it.
evidence.period_fit: Audit was commissioned before and finalized during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution for the commissioning decision; the underlying irregularities are company-level but within a state asset under presidential oversight.
contrary_evidence: The audit concerns a state company with legacy problems and does not prove personal wrongdoing by Tshisekedi.

evidence.claim: The EITI Board said DRC implementation generated tangible reforms with impetus from the Presidency, but also found beneficial-ownership rules only partly implemented and expressed concern about prosecutions of whistle-blowers.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Board said DRC implementation generated tangible reforms with impetus from the Presidency, but also found beneficial-ownership rules only partly implemented and expressed concern about prosecutions of whistle-blowers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: EITI validation is an authoritative external assessment combining performance and remaining gaps.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 validation outcome within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution for presidency-driven follow-through; partial implementation limits the strength of the positive inference.
contrary_evidence: Beneficial ownership remained incomplete and whistleblower prosecutions cut against clean implementation.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said Congolese authorities took no disciplinary action and did not investigate police involvement in the Buhene attacks, and that Tshisekedi later appointed the police commander in charge at the time as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.title: DR Congo: No Inquiry into Police Role in Ethnic Killings
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said Congolese authorities took no disciplinary action and did not investigate police involvement in the Buhene attacks, and that Tshisekedi later appointed the police commander in charge at the time as deputy territory administrator.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report provides a specific accountability failure and a ruler-linked appointment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High attribution for the appointment decision; the lack of inquiry reflects authority exercised under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The article concerns a localized security episode, not the whole governing program.

evidence.claim: DW reported that several close associates of Tshisekedi were accused of corruption, that Tshisekedi had not yet reacted, and that Vidiye Tshimanga resigned after a video showed him negotiating a commission on a mining contract with fake investors.
evidence.title: Des proches de Tshisekedi accusés de corruption
evidence.excerpt: DW reported that several close associates of Tshisekedi were accused of corruption, that Tshisekedi had not yet reacted, and that Vidiye Tshimanga resigned after a video showed him negotiating a commission on a mining contract with fake investors.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting captures the network-level scandal and the president's lack of immediate response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the conduct is network-level, and the article specifically notes the president had not reacted at publication time.
contrary_evidence: The story centers on associates, so it is weaker for direct personal attribution than for network-control inference.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
